summary: The plan editor's canvas (`floor_editor.js`) is now a real pan/zoom viewport instead of a full-size canvas scrolled by the wrapper's native scrollbars: the canvas fills the stage and the plan is drawn through a view transform (`{scale, tx, ty}`), so middle-mouse drag or Space+drag pans, the wheel zooms to the cursor (Ctrl/⌘+wheel still works, for existing muscle memory), `Home` frames the whole plan and `.` frames the current selection - all gestures the old scrollbar-driven canvas could not offer. Snapping, previously invisible, always-on and grid-only, is now a magnet with grid/vertex/edge/midpoint/off modes cycled by `M` or a toolbar button, `Ctrl` inverts the current mode while held, and whatever point is actually caught is drawn on the canvas. A new **Set scale** tool lets an operator drag along a run of known real-world length and type that length in metres, computing the plan's metres-per-pixel directly - `FloorPlan.Scale` defaults to unset (0), and every metre-valued field in the product was previously dead until it was set via a spinner labelled "metres per grid cell". A new status bar (`FloorEditor`'s `onStatus` callback, rendered by `plan_workspace.js` into the existing `.pw-status` strip) reports the active tool, selection count, cursor position (metres once a plan has a scale, pixels until then), snap mode, zoom, and a live hint of what the mouse/keyboard do right now. New modal keyboard accelerators `G`/`R`/`S` (move/rotate/scale) let an operator type an exact value (metres when a scale exists), lock an axis with `X`/`Y`, and confirm/cancel with `Enter`/`Esc`; they are accelerators only, sharing the same `moveRef`/preview/commit path as a mouse drag via a newly extracted `commitMove()`, and are advertised in the status bar rather than hidden in an undiscoverable keymap. The viewport chrome in `fleet-map.css` (dark surround, light plan sheet, flat compact panels, hairline dock seams) now covers the whole `.pw-shell` (header, area bar, palette, status bar) rather than only `.floor-editor` - a deliberate deviation from the original plan, recorded in `docs/MYSELIASAN_PLAN_EDITOR_PLAN.md`, taken because scoping it to the canvas alone produced a half-lit window. New i18n keys (`grid.setScale*`, `grid.frameAll`, `grid.frameSel`, `grid.snapCycle`, `grid.snap.*`, `grid.statusHint`, `grid.modal.*`, `grid.modalHint`, `grid.modalFree`) were added to en/ms/zh/ar. This is phase P2 of the plan editor overhaul plan; no model or API change.
compatibility: Frontend-only; no API, schema, or config change. Existing installs get the new viewport/snap/status-bar behavior automatically on the next frontend build/deploy - no migration, no data change. A plan without a scale set behaves exactly as before (readouts show pixels, metre-only fields stay inert) until an operator runs the new Set scale tool; nothing is set automatically. Dragging objects with the mouse is unchanged - G/R/S are additive accelerators over the same commit path, not a replacement for it.
